subject: general
question: Who among the following pioneered the movement in the support of widow remarriage and girls’ education in Andhra region?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Kandukuri Veeresalingam Pantulu.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kandukuri Veeresalingam Pantulu:-**

 
 
• **He was a renowned social reformer and writer, played a pivotal role in pioneering the movement for widow remarriage and girls' education in the Andhra region of India. **
 
• He is widely regarded as the "Father of the Telugu Renaissance Movement" for his transformative efforts to uplift society.
 
• In 1881, Veeresalingam boldly organized and performed the first widow remarriage in Andhra Pradesh, defying the staunch opposition of conservative elements.
 
• This groundbreaking event marked a turning point in the movement for social reform.
 
• **Veeresalingam established schools for girls, advocating for their education and emphasizing the importance of literacy for women's empowerment. He also founded the "Hithakarini School" in 1908, a residential school specifically for girls.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Chembeti Sridharalu Naidu:-**

 
 
• He was a prominent social reformer and writer in the Telugu-speaking region of India. He was born in 1826 in the village of Chembeti, near Rajahmundry, Andhra Pradesh.
 
• He was educated at a local school and then went on to study law in Madras.
 
 
 
• **Sree Narayana Guru:-**
 
 
• He was a renowned philosopher, social reformer, and spiritual leader in India.
 
• He played a pivotal role in advocating for social justice, equality, and spiritual enlightenment, particularly in the caste-ridden society of Kerala.
 
• His life and teachings continue to inspire and guide people worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Chakravarti Rajagopalachari:-**
 
 
• He was popularly known as Rajaji or C.R., was a prominent Indian statesman, writer, lawyer, and independence activist.
 
• He held various positions of power, including Governor-General of India, Chief Minister of Madras Presidency, Governor of West Bengal, and Minister for Home Affairs of the Indian Union.
